QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_10

question.text: The SPAN margin system considers which of the following risk factors in its scenarios?

answer.text: Price changes and volatility changes of the underlying asset
Only the current market price of the derivative
The credit rating of the trading member
The trading volume of the derivative contract

explanation.text: The Logic: SPAN (Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk) is a portfolio-based margining system that estimates the largest reasonably expected one-day loss on a derivatives portfolio. In standard industry usage it does this by re-pricing the portfolio under a fixed set of risk scenarios that vary the two key drivers of derivatives P&L — the price of the underlying and its volatility — and uses the worst loss across those scenarios as the basis for initial margin. The Trap: SPAN does not key off the current derivative price alone, the credit rating of a member, or the contract's trading volume. Those are not the inputs to its risk scenarios; price movement and volatility movement are. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (160-161) describe SPAN as identifying overall portfolio risk and the largest reasonably expected one-day loss, but the specific "16 scenarios varying price and volatility factors" wording was not located in those pages. The framing above reflects general industry/clearing-corporation documentation of SPAN rather than a direct workbook citation.
